stages.title: CHANGE WITHOUT CONSTITUTIONAL DESTRUCTION

groups.heading: THREE ROUTES
items: Simple-majority constitutional change lies outside Article 368.
Most amendments use the dual special majority.
Entrenched federal subjects also need ratification by at least half of States.

groups.heading: POWER DISTINCTION
items: Ordinary legislative power changes law within competence.
Constituent power changes constitutional text.
Article 368 permits addition, variation or repeal.

groups.heading: SUBSTANTIVE LIMIT
items: Every provision is amendable.
Basic structure protects constitutional identity.
The power to amend is not a power to destroy or replace the Constitution.

stages.answer_line: India does not adopt the United Kingdom's ordinary-legislation model for every constitutional change or the United States' high federal ratification threshold for every amendment.

stages.title: ARTICLE 368 PROCEDURE AND DUAL MAJORITY

groups.heading: INTRODUCTION
items: Bill may originate in either House.
Minister or private member may introduce it.
No prior Presidential recommendation is required.

groups.heading: PASSAGE
items: Each House separately satisfies both majority limbs.
Failure in either House ends the Bill.
There is no joint sitting.

groups.heading: COMPLETION
items: Required States ratify the passed text when the proviso applies.
States cannot amend the Bill.
After due passage, the President shall assent.

stages.answer_line: Article 107(5) states that a Bill pending in Rajya Sabha which Lok Sabha has not passed does not lapse merely because Lok Sabha is dissolved.

stages.title: FEDERAL RATIFICATION: THE EXACT PROVISO LIST

groups.heading: FEDERAL ORGANS
items: Election of President: Articles 54 and 55.
Union and State executive power: Articles 73 and 162.
Supreme Court and High Court chapters.

groups.heading: POWER DISTRIBUTION
items: Chapter I of Part XI.
Any Seventh Schedule List.
Representation of States in Parliament.

groups.heading: SELF-ENTRENCHMENT / LIMIT
items: Article 368 itself.
At least half, not all, States ratify.
Federal consequence alone does not trigger ratification.

stages.answer_line: The list protects the federal bargain by requiring State consent where an amendment changes the Union-State constitutional compact or the States' voice in national institutions.

stages.title: CASE CHRONOLOGY: AMENDABILITY TO CONSTITUTIONAL IDENTITY

pills.text: INDIRA NEHRU GANDHI V. RAJ NARAIN (1975)

groups.heading: AMENDABILITY CONFLICT
items: Shankari Prasad (1951) and Sajjan Singh (1964) allowed FR amendment.
I.C. Golaknath (1967) denied that power.
The 24th Amendment restored constituent-power language.

groups.heading: IDENTITY LIMIT
items: Kesavananda Bharati (1973): amend every provision, damage no basic structure.
Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) protected democratic elections and review.
Minerva Mills (1980) protected limited power and FR-DPSP harmony.

groups.heading: NINTH SCHEDULE EXTENSION
items: Waman Rao (1980) fixed 24 April 1973 as cut-off.
I.R. Coelho (2007) required impact review after the cut-off.
Judicial review remains part of the protected identity.

stages.answer_line: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) replaced an absolute bar on amending Fundamental Rights with a judicially enforceable limit protecting the Constitution's basic identity.

stages.title: BASIC-STRUCTURE ELEMENTS: NON-EXHAUSTIVE AND CASE-ATTRIBUTED

groups.heading: GOVERNMENT FORM
items: Constitutional supremacy.
Republican and democratic government.
Free and fair elections; secularism; federalism.

groups.heading: LEGAL ARCHITECTURE
items: Separation of powers and rule of law.
Judicial review and judicial independence.
Limited amending power.

groups.heading: RIGHTS AND BALANCE
items: Dignity, liberty and equality within the rights architecture.
Harmony between Fundamental Rights and DPSP.
The list is illustrative, not closed or unanimously authored.

stages.answer_line: Different judges in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) proposed overlapping lists; the narrow majority ratio is the limitation on destruction of basic structure, not one unanimous catalogue.

stages.title: NINTH SCHEDULE: POST-1973 IMPACT REVIEW

groups.heading: ORIGIN
items: The First Amendment inserted Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule.
Listing supplied a protective constitutional device.
Placement occurs through constitutional amendment.

groups.heading: CUT-OFF AND TEST
items: Waman Rao (1980) fixes 24 April 1973.
I.R. Coelho (2007) reviews post-cut-off insertions.
The inquiry asks whether protected Part III principles suffer basic-structure damage.

groups.heading: TRAPS
items: Reviewability is not automatic invalidity.
Listing is not permanent immunity.
Pre-cut-off status does not erase every other constitutional issue.

stages.answer_line: Article 31B validates the Acts and Regulations placed in the Ninth Schedule notwithstanding inconsistency with Part III, subject to later basic-structure review of the constitutional amendment that grants that protection.

stages.title: ANJUM KADARI (2024): THE ORDINARY-STATUTE BOUNDARY

groups.heading: AMENDMENT REVIEW
items: Constitutional amendments face direct basic-structure review.
The inquiry arises from Article 368 limits.
Damage to identity is the substantive test.

groups.heading: ORDINARY-LAW REVIEW
items: Ordinary laws are tested through competence, Part III and other provisions.
Basic features can guide interpretation.
They do not become a free-standing super-Article.

groups.heading: EXAM CORRECTION
items: Identify Article X embodying the feature.
Do not invalidate a statute only through an undefined structural slogan.
Anjum Kadari (2024) supplies the current boundary.

stages.answer_line: Tribunal cases may use separation of powers and judicial independence, but the statutory defect should be connected to Articles governing judicial review, equality, court substitution or another express constitutional command.

stages.title: CURRENT CONTROLS AND THE JUDICIAL-SUPREMACY DEBATE

groups.heading: 106TH AMENDMENT
items: S.O. 1922(E) commenced the framework on 16 April 2026.
Article 334A still requires census publication and delimitation.
Commencement does not mean operational reservation.

groups.heading: 131ST BILL
items: The 2026 Bill was negatived in Lok Sabha.
It illustrates dual-majority arithmetic.
It is not law, precedent or a current seat ceiling.

groups.heading: EVALUATION
items: Identity review protects future democracy and limited government.
Critics stress uncertainty and judicial supremacy.
Discipline requires text, precedent, actual damage and narrow remedy.

stages.answer_line: Although the 106th Amendment commenced, Article 334A postpones operational reservation until post-commencement census figures are published and delimitation is completed.

stages.title: FINAL SYNTHESIS: TRAPS, PYQS AND ANSWER SPINE

groups.heading: PRELIMS CONTROL
items: No joint sitting; President shall assent.
Ratification applies to the exact proviso list.
Basic structure is non-exhaustive; post-1973 listing is reviewable.

groups.heading: PYQ ROUTES
items: 2 Mains and 8 Prelims are verified.
2024 Q66 official local key is D.
2025 Q58 official local key is A; older keys remain inferred.

groups.heading: MAINS LADDER
items: Distinguish the three change routes.
State exact procedure and case chronology.
Apply Ninth Schedule and ordinary-law boundaries.
Evaluate flexibility, federal consent and judicial review.

stages.mechanism_strip: A complete answer separates procedure from substantive identity, applies exact doctrine and ends with a qualified flexibility-versus-rigidity verdict.
stages.answer_line: The power is nevertheless limited: an amendment cannot damage, destroy or abrogate the Constitution's basic structure or framework.

stages.title: OPTIONAL ENRICHMENT: AMENDMENT VERSUS REPLACEMENT

groups.heading: ENRICHMENT
items: Amendment preserves legal continuity; replacement claims a new constituent foundation.
Comparative systems use text, eternity clauses or judicial doctrine.

groups.heading: USE WITH DISCIPLINE
items: Comparative analogy cannot replace Indian cases.
State ratification remains textually limited.
Add only after the full Indian core is secure.
